title: Testing history
description: Each research phase: the question, method, finding and decision.

rows.name: Exit replay
rows.question: Why are wins smaller than losses (avg win under $1, avg loss over $1)?
rows.method: Replayed the bot's 95 trades from the last 48h on 1-minute Binance candles under 8 trailing-stop widths and 4 stop distances.
rows.finding: The trailing stop closed winners on a ~0.17% pullback while stops ran ~1.1%. Wider trails grew wins but turned more trades into stop-losses; tighter stops were worse. No exit rule made the trades profitable.
rows.decision: Keep exits roughly as they are; switch the trail to a fixed 0.5% of price.

rows.name: Trailing stop change
rows.question: Make the trail independent of leverage.
rows.method: New setting trail_reversal_raw_pct = 0.50 used by the live exit loop and the daily baseline tool; 3 new unit tests.
rows.finding: Shipped and running since the Oct 16 restart. Nothing committed yet.
rows.decision: Monitor; this is a small improvement, not a fix.

rows.name: Signal and setup scan
rows.question: Do any of the bot's signals or researcher setups predict direction?
rows.method: 21,600 researcher packets, 41,000 ML predictions and 794 trades compared with the real move 15, 30 and 60 minutes later, grouped by every indicator, setup, confidence level and derivatives reading.
rows.finding: Nothing clears the 0.13% round-trip cost. The best-looking groups were shorts in a falling market. Highest researcher confidence was the least accurate; long trades were right only 43.6% of the time.

rows.name: BTC trend filter and longer holds
rows.question: Does trading with BTC's trend, or holding 4h to 24h, create an edge?
rows.method: Same signals checked at 1h, 4h and 24h, split by BTC trend; simple trend rules tested on a year of 1h candles for 440 coins.
rows.finding: Only shorting during the recent decline made money. Trading with BTC's 4h direction roughly halved trade losses but stayed negative. Trend rules lost at 4h in every quarter.

rows.name: Independent strategy research
rows.question: Which known crypto strategies have evidence of working after costs?
rows.method: Literature review plus backtests on daily candles for 657 Binance perpetuals (2021 to 2026) and funding history for the top 150.
rows.finding: Weekly trend-following on the 10 major coins was the only robust result. Funding carry pays little now; reversal, low-volatility and funding-contrarian strategies lose.
rows.decision: Shortlist five strategies for a head-to-head test.

rows.name: Five shortlisted strategies
rows.question: How do the shortlisted strategies compare under one framework?
rows.method: Same data, costs, funding and metrics for each, plus a parameter grid to measure robustness and a 3x cost stress test.
rows.finding: Trend on majors (long or flat) held up in 93% of settings. Cross-coin momentum was unstable; BTC-to-alt lead-lag lost in every setting.
rows.decision: Trend on majors is the lead candidate.

rows.name: Day-trading setups with risk rules
rows.question: Do the five supplied day-trading setups work under strict risk rules?
rows.method: Liquidity sweep and FVG, VWAP, volume profile with delta, breakouts, and liquidation flush coded as rules on BTC, ETH and SOL 5-minute candles (2024 to 2026), with 1% risk, hard stops, 5x cap, 3R daily limit and London/NY session only. Compared against random entries.
rows.finding: All five lose. Their edge before costs is close to random entries, and costs take 0.3R to 0.7R per trade because 5-minute stops are so tight. Breakeven moves and partial exits made results worse.

rows.name: Trend strategy: rules and backtest check
rows.question: Does the live code reproduce the research, and which risk rules should it use?
rows.method: Strategy rules coded as a shared module with 10 unit tests, then a 2021-2026 day-by-day simulation through that code with real fills, real funding, Binance minimum order sizes, disaster stops and the kill switch, starting from $450.
rows.finding: Matches the research (2022-2025 and worst drawdown identical). With all rules: +26.5% a year, Sharpe 1.14, worst drawdown -25.8%; 2025 +1.6%, 2026 so far -3.1%. A -25% stop fired 63 times on crash wicks and cost about 4% a year; -40% fired 15 times and costs about 1.5%. Re-sizing positions between rebalances cost about 3% a year. The kill switch never triggered.
rows.decision: Use a -40% stop (inside the 2x liquidation level) and hold quantities between rebalances.

rows.name: Side-by-side paper test
rows.question: Does the trend strategy beat the current bot on live paper data?
rows.method: Trend strategy runs as its own paper bot (separate service and tables) next to the unchanged current bot. Both started from $511.82, the current bot's equity at launch. The trend bot checks funding and stops hourly and rebalances every 5 days; a snapshot of both balances is taken daily.
rows.finding: Started Oct 16, 22:41 UTC. Initial rebalance on the Oct 15 close: 7 longs (BTC, SOL, XRP, ADA, LINK, LTC, AVAX), about 42% of equity. First scheduled rebalance on the Oct 17 close. Results will be added here weekly.
rows.decision: Review after 6 to 8 weeks (8 to 11 rebalances).
